title: Remove Every Value That Occurs More Than Once

concept.title: A tail pointer that lags behind the scan
body: In the easy problem one copy of every value stayed. Now **every node whose value occurs more than once** must go, so a whole group of equal values is deleted, and the group may start at the head. Use a **dummy** node and a reference `prev` to the **last node that is kept**. Look at the group that starts at `prev.next`: if it has more than one node, skip it completely, otherwise keep the node.

body.code:
dummy = ListNode(0, head)
prev = dummy
while head is not None:
    if head.next is not None and head.val == head.next.val:
        value = head.val
        while head is not None and head.val == value:   # skip the whole group
            head = head.next
        prev.next = head
    else:
        prev = head                                       # a single node: keep it
        head = head.next
return dummy.next

body: `prev` is not moved when a group is skipped, because the node after the group may start a new group that has to be skipped too.

statement: A singly linked list is sorted in non-decreasing order. Delete all nodes that have a value that appears more than once in the list, so that only the values that occur exactly once remain. Print the resulting list, or `empty` if nothing remains.
inputFormat: The first line has `n`, the number of nodes. The second line has the values of the nodes, from the head to the tail. The values are in non-decreasing order.
outputFormat: Print the values of the new list on one line, or `empty`.

examples.note: The values 3 and 4 occur twice and are removed: 1 2 5.

hints: Use a dummy node and a reference to the last node that is kept.
If the current node has the same value as the next one, skip the whole group of this value.
Only move the `prev` reference when you keep a node.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

# Every node is also remembered in this list. Python in the browser cannot free a very long chain of nodes at once,
# so free_nodes() (called at the end) cuts the links first and the nodes are then freed one by one.
all_nodes = []


class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next
        all_nodes.append(self)


def free_nodes():
    for node in all_nodes:
        node.next = None
        if hasattr(node, "random"):
            node.random = None
    all_nodes.clear()


# Builds a list from the values. If pos is 0 or more, the last node points back to the node at index pos (a cycle).
def build_list(values, pos=-1):
    head = None
    for v in reversed(values):
        head = ListNode(v, head)
    if pos >= 0:
        tail = head
        while tail.next is not None:
            tail = tail.next
        target = head
        for _ in range(pos):
            target = target.next
        tail.next = target
    return head


# Prints the values of a list on one line ("empty" for an empty list).
def print_list(head):
    out = []
    while head is not None:
        out.append(head.val)
        head = head.next
    print(*(out if out else ["empty"]))

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

print_list(delete_all_duplicates(build_list(a)))
free_nodes()

explanation: `prev` marks the last kept node. A group of equal values is skipped as a whole and `prev.next` jumps behind it; a single node is kept and `prev` moves on.
